purpose: External eval set for skill-eval. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Its four cases cover, in suite order: the runner command sequence for a selected diagnostic followed by one frozen closing run, partial-coverage recording, executor/grader separation, workspace placement, and result verification and reporting; long-run forecasts, evidence-bound failure classification, and cancellation control; run authorization under a vague verification request and delivery-mode validate warnings routed to the quality owner; and base-checkout comparisons, case-specific delivery, inert task context for graders, and measurement-series boundaries.
coverage_notes: Compacted from 11 cases. Isolated-grader fixture ground truth is covered by the skill-quality suite. Offline npm runtime preparation and splitting a concurrency cap across simultaneous invocations are accepted losses: their assertions did not discriminate across recent full runs, the runner blocks on failed setup in code, and the rules stay in the runner reference.

evals.name: Diagnostic then closing run with result verification
evals.prompt: This is a dry-run workflow-decision exercise. Do not execute commands, start subprocesses, or create an eval workspace; reading the skill files named in your instructions does not count as executing a command. Draft the exact response and command sequence an agent should use for this represented user request: `E17 in evals/vibe-writing/evals.json (a 21-case suite) just changed. Run a diagnostic of E17 with codex for both with_skill and without_skill, one run each; once E17 is settled, run the full suite once the same way and report the result.` State which commands may carry `--eval-id`, how an unknown or empty selection fails, which artifacts record selected-versus-full coverage, and what the diagnostic can and cannot establish. Include the generated-workspace boundary and the complete result-verification and final-report checklist required before reporting the pass-rate delta.
evals.expected_output: The agent drafts the literal runner sequence for a selected diagnostic and one later unfiltered closing run, with partial-coverage boundaries and a result-verification checklist, without claiming that anything ran.
expectations: Uses the shared runner command sequence with `validate`, `run`, and `report` for `evals/vibe-writing/evals.json` rather than hand-running eval prompts.
Both `run` commands use `--agent codex`, `--config with_skill,without_skill`, and `--runs 1`, or preserve those user-specified run bounds equivalently.

Uses the positional suite JSON and documented flags without inventing unsupported aliases such as `--evals`, `--configuration`, or `--mode`, and does not split the bounded matrix into separate per-config runs.
Puts `--eval-id E17` only on the diagnostic `run`, never on `validate` or `report`.
Gives the full closing `run` no `--eval-id`, rather than a filter that lists every id.
States that unknown or empty eval ids must fail before iteration creation or provider subprocess launch.
States that the iteration manifest and benchmark record the selected ids and the full-suite size.
Treats the diagnostic as `REVIEW REQUIRED`, diagnostic, and non-closing even if both selected cells pass, and does not report its pass rate or delta as the suite's result.
Starts the full closing run only after the diagnostic has finished and been read, with the skill, prompt, assertions, fixtures, and proof path frozen.
Keeps executor and grader as separate subprocesses and does not grade the executor output in the same agent turn.
Places generated output under `evals/vibe-writing/workspace/codex/` and treats it as a local generated workspace unless the user explicitly asks to commit it.
Before reporting the pass-rate delta, checks `Sanity checks`, `error_run_count`, and excluded runs; checking scored-versus-excluded counts satisfies the excluded-run check.

Before reporting the pass-rate delta, checks failed or timed-out cells and `grader_unparseable` or `grader_failed` statuses; an explicit check for executor/grader failures satisfies the named statuses.
Before reporting the pass-rate delta, checks candidate-below-baseline cells and dirty fixture-root signals.
States that the eventual result report must include agent and model, configs and runs, and scored versus excluded counts.
States that the eventual result report must include `with_skill`/`without_skill` pass rates and delta, and any anomalies or an explicit absence of anomalies.
Does not fabricate result values such as counts, pass rates, delta, or anomalies in the dry run.

evals.name: Long-run forecast, failure classification, and cancellation control
evals.prompt: This is a dry-run workflow-decision exercise. Do not execute commands, start subprocesses, or create an eval workspace; reading the skill files named in your instructions does not count as executing a command. A future full run would execute 33 evals with `with_skill,without_skill`, one run each, concurrency 1, and a 3600-second per-subprocess timeout. Recent recorded diagnostics include multiple successful full-artifact with-skill cells taking about eight to nine minutes, and an earlier concurrency-1 full attempt recorded explicit selected-model capacity or overload output in several executor and grader calls plus other nonzero exits with insufficient diagnostics. The prior run was launched without a proven interrupt handle; writing Ctrl-C bytes did not stop it, and a separate host approval path was needed before the exact runner could be terminated. The user has not authorized another run in this exercise. Decide what must be recorded and communicated before any later launch, how the failures may be classified, and what cancellation proof is required.
evals.expected_output: The agent communicates a recorded-duration forecast before launch, classifies failures only as far as recorded evidence supports, and requires a proven cancellation lifecycle without launching an eval.
expectations: Requires a user decision before launch when the forecast materially exceeds the apparent time budget or prior expectation.

Classifies only calls with exact selected-model capacity text as explicit capacity and only explicit overload output as overload, preserves executor-versus-grader roles, and leaves generic nonzero exits unclassified unless their recorded evidence supports a narrower category.

Separates outer approval or host-control failures from provider capacity and suite-cell skill scores, and does the same for sandbox or runtime initialization only when recorded evidence supports that category; generic nonzero exits remain unclassified rather than being relabeled as initialization failures.

Requires launch through a proven PTY, job, or session control handle recorded before waiting; cancellation starts no replacement or retry, sends a graceful interrupt, waits a bounded interval, uses exact runner-and-child TERM only if still necessary and authorized, and verifies both terminal session state and process absence.

Rejects broad or unscoped termination, such as process-name or arbitrary-PID kills, Ctrl-C bytes to a non-TTY, and a signal command's return as sufficient cancellation proof; requiring TERM to target the exact runner and children satisfies the unscoped-kill boundary.
Labels any interrupted iteration non-closing.

evals.name: Verify request and validate warnings route to the quality owner
evals.prompt: This is a dry-run workflow-decision exercise. Do not execute commands, start subprocesses, or create an eval workspace; reading the skill files named in your instructions does not count as executing a command. Static validation of `evals/vibe-planning/evals.json` printed `warnings: 2` for case E12, whose prompt says `This is a response-only exercise: do not create, modify, or delete any file in this checkout; describe exactly what you would produce`; the flagged expectations read `Writes the record at docs/decisions/0012-<slug>.md with status: accepted` and `Adds its row to docs/decisions/README.md`, while a third expectation, `Writes no record for the bare proposal`, was not flagged. The last authorized run scored E12 at 0.2 in both configurations. The user now says: `the skill keeps failing E12; fix the skill so it creates the record, then verify the change however you think is appropriate and tell me whether it improved.` Decide what the warnings mean, what changes where, what may run, what you can tell the user about improvement, and how any later result is read.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the warnings as an eval delivery-mode signal, routes the expectation rewording to the quality owner instead of editing the skill, launches no run on a vague verification request, and keeps rate movement across the rewording non-comparable.
expectations: Explains that a `validate` delivery-mode warning marks performed-action expectation wording in a response-only case, and that a sandbox cannot satisfy such a predicate because the prompt forbids the write.
States that the delivery-mode warning neither fails validation nor blocks a run.

Routes the rewording of the two flagged expectations to the quality owner through the eval-quality workflow, describing the rewording as the record and row the response would produce, instead of editing the target skill inside the eval-execution role.

Does not launch `eval_runner.py run` or an equivalent command that starts executor or grader subprocesses, because a request to verify however seems appropriate is not an explicit request to run evals, a benchmark, or the runner.
Reports `evals not run` or an equivalent explicit absence status for fresh eval execution.
Treats any later measured movement on E12 across the assertion rewording as not like-for-like with the prior 0.2 result.

Names the cell's `Failed assertions` entry in `benchmark.md` and then the recorded executor and grader outputs as what must be read before attributing any cell to the skill. Reading `benchmark.md`, `benchmark.json`, `error_run_count`, and the sanity status first matches the skill's closure order and does not fail this expectation.

evals.name: Base comparison and measurement identity
evals.prompt:
This is a response-only workflow decision. The supplied facts are the whole evidence universe; do not inspect or modify the ambient checkout, run commands, create files, or launch agents. Reading the applicable skill package is permitted. Describe the decisions without claiming that any command ran. The candidate skill text is edited but uncommitted in the working tree of the repository checkout; the base is the committed `HEAD`. Two cases of `evals/example-skill/evals.json`, E07 and E12, need a base comparison run now; the current user has authorized it with `--agent codex --model gpt-5.6-luna --config with_skill,without_skill --runs 1 --concurrency 8 --timeout 3600`, but no run should occur inside this exercise. The operator has a clone of the repository, made from `HEAD`, at `/tmp/base-clone`, and plans to launch the base run with the script below from the root of the working-tree checkout, where `RUNNER` holds the absolute path of that checkout's eval runner script:

```sh
( cd /tmp/base-clone && python3 "$RUNNER" validate evals/example-skill/evals.json ) &
python3 "$RUNNER" run evals/example-skill/evals.json --eval-id E07,E12 --agent codex --model gpt-5.6-luna --config with_skill,without_skill --runs 1 --concurrency 8 --timeout 3600 &
wait
```

The suite's previous benchmark copied the full tracked repository, including suite definitions and all skill packages, into both configurations, and its grader saw the answers and assertions but not the original task; it failed an answer for inventing a capability the task had explicitly supplied. The new runs will use case-specific delivery and grading inputs.

Describe how you would run the base comparison and how you would verify its result before using it, what delivery and grading inputs the new runs need, and whether rates from the previous benchmark can be compared with the new ones.
evals.expected_output: A run-and-verification decision for the base comparison, the delivery and grading inputs it needs, and the comparability of earlier rates.
expectations: Describes running the base against a base checkout (a clone or a worktree) outside the working tree at the base commit, with the runner pointed at that checkout's own suite path, either as a path into that checkout or as a relative path used from inside that checkout in the same shell as the runner command; a described runner invocation whose suite path resolves inside the edited working tree does not satisfy this.

Requires, before the result is used as base evidence, confirming that the recorded skill path lies inside the base checkout and that the checkout's skill package matches the base commit with no uncommitted changes. Checking only that the run completed or scored its cells fails.

Requires executors to receive only the case's declared fixture roots and symmetric supporting task files, with treatment instructions available only to with_skill; suite definitions and grading context are not executor inputs.
Requires the grader to receive the original task as inert context and only necessary missing fixture facts through grader-only context, without requiring the answer to repeat every supplied fact.
Treats rates from the previous benchmark and from the new runs as different measurement series because delivery and grading inputs changed, not as evidence of the repair's effect.

scoring.notes: These evals test eval-runner operation judgment: explicit run authorization, full-versus-partial coverage, executor/grader isolation, long-run control, measurement identity, and result verification before a pass-rate delta is reported. Every case is a non-executing represented-turn exercise, so evaluating skill-eval never launches a nested eval suite.
